answer: A seismic-coupling protocol curbs Sybil attacks among agents monitoring oil shale basins. Verifiers emit acoustic pulses through bedrock, requiring nodes to sign localized elastodynamic reflections with an internal cipher. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of deploying discrete geophone probes per identity, making costless cloning a physical fable. However, microseisms and fracturing introduce baseline noise, causing occasional false rejections.
